cues.say: Component 5: Object storage. Cloud storage for files, each saved under a name. Cheap and practically unlimited. The database keeps only the file's name. You'll bring this up during version one, when you draw the basic design.
Think of it as: Google Drive for your app. Use it for photos, PDFs, videos, and exports.
Here's a real scenario. A print-shop customer uploads 10 photos (4 megabytes each) for holiday cards.
Without it: 40 megabytes per order passes through the API servers.
Thousands of orders clog servers and bloat the database.
With it: API hands the browser 10 signed upload links.
Browser sends photos straight to storage.
Database keeps the names; a worker fetches photos to print.
Why it works: Storage is built for big files; your servers and database aren't.
In the interview, say: The browser uploads straight to storage with a signed URL, so photos never pass through our servers.
A few related terms you may hear.
Signed URL: A temporary link to upload or download one file directly.
CDN: Serve stored files through it.
